metadata.case_name: TSUI KIM MING v. CHARTER FORM CO. LTD.

plaintiff.occupation_before: involved in waterproofing work as a construction site worker; employed as a foreman in 1997

injuries.description: Injury to left index finger: 4 cm laceration over the dorsal side exposing the proximal interphalangeal joint; deep cut of the extensor tendon; fractures of the proximal and middle phalanges; fusion of the PIP joint.
source: the Plaintiff suffered a 4 cm laceration over the dorsal side of his left index finger, exposing the proximal interphalangeal joint.
There was a cut, a deep cut, of the extensor tendon.
There were fractures of the proximal and middle phalanges of the left index finger.
I find that the plaintiff has suffered 6 per cent of impairment of the whole person by reason of an injury to his finger, left index finger.
injuries.icd_description: Injury of multiple sites of hand

manifestations.description: Decrease in grip power which would be permanent
Mild to moderate reduction in his working capacity and efficiency
Difficulty in buttoning his shirt (slowness), stiffness or pain when the weather is cold
Handicap in the labour market: more difficult to get a job and more liable to be laid off or sacked

treatments_received: operation to repair cut extensor tendon (performed on date of accident)
fusion (treatment of fractures close to the PIP joint) with immobilisation in a splint for about eight months until May 1999
removal of implanted K-wire in December 1998
24 sessions of physiotherapy from 8 October 1998 to 16 March 1999
4 sessions of occupational therapy from 16 March 1999 to 23 July 1999

losses.description: Pain, suffering and loss of amenities of life (award under this head $350,000).

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Difficulty in buttoning his shirt; slowness and stiffness/pain in cold weather affecting daily activities.
Handicap in the labour market resulting in more difficulty getting a job and greater risk of being laid off; loss of earning capacity (award $100,000).
